description:
FILED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5 CHECK 2, as a BUNDLE BY
POPULATION and explicitly not as one bug: every row below carries this number
so the census has a cause, and each bullet is independently sizeable.  Split it
when one is picked up.

t/io/open.t -- 36 rows, four shapes:
  * NUL IN A PATHNAME (18 rows): perl 5.18+ refuses `open`/`chmod`/`glob`/
    `unlink` on a path containing "\0" with a "Invalid \\0 character in
    pathname" WARNING and a false return; PCL accepts it.  Includes the
    `(overload)` twins (an object whose `""` produces the NUL).
  * AUTOVIV FH THROUGH AN ELEMENT (4 rows): `open $a[0], ...` / `open $h{x},
    ...` must autovivify a handle into the ARRAY/HASH slot, package and lexical.
  * BAD LAYER / BAD MODE WARNINGS (5 rows): `>>>`, `>:u`, `<:u`, `:c` --
    perl WARNS and fails; PCL fails silently (the #221 family).
  * IN-MEMORY BUFFERING (2 rows): `buffering delays writing to scalar` -- perl's
    :scalar layer does not make a write visible until the buffer flushes; PCL's
    Gray stream writes through.
  Plus 3 die-message-text rows (NS:Error message text and format) and the 2+2
  `not inherited across exec` rows, which are #1707's fact in this file.
  NOTE: io/open.t reads 152/36 on THIS tree, on a `git archive 2ff53f8d`
  extraction and three times run alone, where the blessed snapshot says 154/34 --
  so 2 rows of PRE-EXISTING, STABLE drift that no one has bisected.  Not
  spliced by s473t5d (a mover I did not cause is not mine to re-bless).

t/io/scalar.t -- 30 rows, in-memory (\$scalar) handles: `check warnings` /
  `should have warned` / `check we did warn` (#221), `$!` after a failed
  in-memory op (`Permission denied` on a read-only scalar, `check errno set`),
  a non-downgradable SV refused on a byte open, `FETCH only called once` on a
  tied scalar target, and `still a ref after opening for appending`.

t/io/argv.t -- 29 rows: `<>`/`<<>>` and @ARGV -- the warning for an @ARGV entry
  that looks like a pipe (`|-`, `-|`, `| -`, `- |`: 16 rows, #221 plus the
  `<<>>` distinction that `<<>>` must NOT treat them as commands), `$.` across
  ARGV files, `eof()` on an unopened handle, and ARGV aliasing.

t/io/pipe.t -- 18 rows (+2 io/openpid.t): fork-pipe children -- `errno` after a
  failed piped open, `status` and `$?` after an implicit close, a child reaped
  when the program cannot be exec'd, and the exception a failing PerlIO raises.
  The file renumbers (7 `extra` rows), so read the alignment before the counts.

t/io/nargv.t -- 7 rows: the in-place edit does NOT PRESERVE THE FILE MODE
  (measured `before 0104600 after 0100664` -- perl copies the original's
  permissions, including the setuid bit, onto the replacement) and PCL emits its
  TAP rows at a different point in the loop, so the file renumbers.

t/io/inplace.t -- the 2-row residue after #1701: `die shouldn't touch file` and
  `last should update file` -- what the in-place edit does on an ABNORMAL exit
  (a die must leave the original, a `last` must still commit).
t/io/iprefix.t -- 2 rows, the same family with `$^I` as a PREFIX ("bak_*")
  rather than a suffix.

t/io/perlio_leaks.t -- 8 rows: the file counts DESCRIPTOR NUMBERS after
  open/`:pop` (`got 5, expected 4`).  PCL's fd numbers are not perl's (SBCL
  holds descriptors of its own) and there is no layer STACK to `:pop` -- the
  latter half is #139.
t/io/crlf.t (6 of 10) / t/io/layers.t (all 55 short) / t/io/perlio_fail.t (4) --
  #139 (`PerlIO::get_layers`) and #221.  io/layers.t additionally shows that a
  BAREWORD in a user function's argument slot (`PerlIO::get_layers(STDIN)`)
  emits a BARE CL SYMBOL and dies "The variable STDIN is unbound" -- perl passes
  the string "STDIN" there; that is the #266/#452 classifier family and is the
  file's actual abort, one layer in front of #139.

t/io/bom.t -- 2 rows: a UTF-16BE/LE BOM at the head of a file must select the
  encoding.  t/io/fs.t -- 2: `skip has futimes` ($Config{d_futimes}) and
  `truncate(word)` must not fall back to a file NAME.  t/io/iofile.t -- 1:
  `IO::File now loaded` ($INC{'IO/File.pm'} after an IO::Handle method).
  t/io/errnosig.t -- 1: a caught signal must not modify `$!`.
  t/io/print.t -- 1: `printf "%n"` is fatal in perl.
  t/io/pvbm.t -- 5: the KNOWN FLAPPER; 23/5 run alone (three times, and on a
  2ff53f8d extraction), 20/8 inside a batch -- the seventh recording of the same
  split.  Not spliced.
  t/io/fflush.t -- 3: #1585.  t/io/data.t -- 1: #1652.
  t/io/semctl.t -- 1: NS:DynaLoader / XS binary extensions (IPC::SysV).
  t/io/utf8.t -- the 9-row residue after #1698: 4 `must warn about bad utf8`
  (#221), 2 `use bytes; length(...)` rows (the PRAGMA half, NS:`use bytes`),
  1 `getc returning non-utf8 after utf8` (a layer change between two getc
  calls), 1 `sprintf "%vd"` malformed-UTF-8 warning (#221), and ONE PARKED row
  (io/utf8.t:251, `isnt(defined $@, !0)` after `no warnings 'utf8'` -- three
  probes vs perl 5.40.3 all MATCH (`undef $@`, a wide print to a byte handle,
  `no warnings 'utf8'` itself), so the cause is upstream in the file's state and
  was not found in the round's budget).

t/run/exit.t -- 3 rows: `${^CHILD_ERROR_NATIVE}` and death-by-signal --
  NS:`fork` caveat 2 (a fork-then-continue child is an SBCL process, so
  `$? & 127` reads 0 where perl shows the signal).
t/run/runenv_randseed.t -- 6: #1236.  t/run/switchC.t -- 12: #1272.
t/run/runenv_hashseed.t -- 269: #1590 (+#1588 behind it).
t/run/runenv.t -- TRANSPILE-FAIL, 106 rows: #1582.
t/run/locale.t -- 1 row + 44 short: #1705.

=== SPLIT THIS OUT FIRST: an UNDECLARED BAREWORD in a user sub's ARGUMENT SLOT
=== is emitted as a BARE CL SYMBOL READ -- neither of perl's two answers
Found s473t5d while looking for t/io/layers.t's abort, which is
`PerlIO::get_layers(STDIN)`.  It is not about that file at all -- it has a
two-line reproducer and it kills the whole top-level form wherever it occurs.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL HEAD):
    sub f { print "[", (defined $_[0] ? $_[0] : "undef"), "]\n" }
    f(STDIN); f(FOO); f(SOMENAME);
    print "still-running\n";
  perl:  [STDIN] [FOO] [SOMENAME] still-running
  PCL:   dies -- "The variable STDIN is unbound", nothing printed

The emission is `(p-void-ctx (pl-f |stdin|))`: a BARE SYMBOL READ.  Under `no
strict subs` (which is PCL's world -- not-supported.md
"### `use strict 'refs'` is not enforced") perl's answer is the STRING "STDIN".
#266's classifier says a bare NAME is a CALL only where it is CALLABLE, so the
non-callable branch should be the string; a bare variable read is a THIRD thing
and is neither answer.  Note this is NOT the residue DECIDED Â§s470bx accepted:
that ruling is about a lower-case bareword in an EXPR HANDLE slot staying a
CALL (loud, deliberate).  Here nothing is a handle slot and nothing is a call.

WHERE: the same `_word_is_term` / `fh_bareword_shape` family the sibling sites
read (#266, #452, #594, #1231).  Probe the cases it would BREAK: a DECLARED sub
called without parens must stay a CALL; a bareword in an `open`/filetest/`*`
slot must keep its ruled handle-NAME or CALL reading; `=>` and `$h{BAREWORD}`
autoquoting must not change.

ROWS: t/io/layers.t's whole 55-row shortfall sits behind it (one layer in front
of #139, which the file would hit next), and it is the shape of an unknown
number of `(none)` aborts elsewhere -- it was found by accident, not by a scan.
subject: the io/ + run/ RESIDUE of #1501 round 5: eleven files, each with its own measured shape (NUL pathnames, autoviv fh through an element, in-memory handle errno/warnings, <> and @ARGV, the in-place edit's mode and abnormal exit, fd numbering, UTF-16 BOM, printf %n, $! after a signal)
